root_cause: Inventory-service v2.1.0 introduced an unbounded in-memory ProductLookupCache backed by ConcurrentHashMap, keyed by productId plus requestId, with no maximumSize, TTL, or eviction. The feature flag inventory.local_cache.enabled was enabled at 08:32. The cache grows on each lookup, producing a near-linear per-pod memory increase independent of flat request volume. Heap pressure drives longer GC pauses and latency, followed by OOMKilled restarts and a restart loop. The memory limit remained 1Gi and node neighbours remained stable; Redis calls per request fell, showing the cache feature was active.

hypotheses.title: Order-service v2.3.1 deployment caused the issue
Redis memory problem caused inventory failures
Inventory memory limit is too low

expected_timeline.event: Inventory v2.1.0 deployed and local cache flag enabled
Heap crossed 80%; GC and latency begin deteriorating
Full GC repeatedly reclaims only about 3%
First pod OOMKilled again; restart backoff follows

expected_impact.note: Inventory lookup latency degrades before the first restart; short restart windows cause intermittent stock checks and cart failures.

remediation_options.title: Roll back inventory-service to v2.0.4 (RB-INV-204)
remediation_options.why: Removes the newly introduced cache implementation; memory returns to about 44%, restarts stop and downstream errors normalize.

remediation_options.title: Disable inventory.local_cache.enabled and rolling restart
remediation_options.why: Disables the unbounded cache and replaces pods; equivalent mitigation without reverting the whole image.

remediation_options.title: Restart inventory pods only
remediation_options.why: Only temporarily resets memory; the same cache fills again at the accelerated rate.

remediation_options.title: Raise memory limit from 1Gi to 2Gi
remediation_options.why: Delays OOM but leaves unbounded growth in place.

remediation_options.title: Scale inventory replicas from 3 to 6
remediation_options.why: Adds capacity but does not remove the leak.

remediation_options.title: No action
remediation_options.why: OOM loop and downstream impact continue.

smoking_gun_queries.expected_result: All three inventory pods rise at roughly 0.42 percentage points per minute, despite flat lookup request rate.
Full GC lines report only about 3% reclaimed, while heap and p99 latency continue increasing.
v2.1.0 enables the local cache; PR #517 uses unbounded ConcurrentHashMap with no maximumSize, TTL, or eviction.

expected_verification: Rollback to v2.0.4 at 10:58 should return pod memory to approximately 44% and keep it flat; restarts stop and order errors return to normal by 11:06. Disabling the feature flag with a rolling restart is an equally effective lower-risk alternative.
